documents.abstract: Convective storm nowcasting in regions with sparse rain-gauge telemetry faces a structural tension: graph-neural emulators can interpolate storm tracks from incomplete observations, but the calibration bounds that govern their reliability, and the equity of the warning lead times they produce, remain poorly characterised. The analysis treats the gauge network as a graph with known sampling geometry, defines a spectral calibration bound in terms of the graph Laplacian and the emulator's Lipschitz constant, and shows that lead-time disparities between well-observed and sparsely observed catchments are bounded by the same spectral quantity. A worked illustration using NASA POWER monthly reanalysis for Harare, Zimbabwe (2000–2023, 312 monthly observations, mean 18.914 °C, decadal warming trend 0.2001 °C) anchors the calibration discussion in a real reanalysis record. The framework yields three results: a calibration bound that degrades predictably with gauge density, a lead-time equity condition that fails when spectral gap ratios exceed a threshold, and a set of design constraints for gauge augmentation. The contribution is a bounded, testable account of when graph-neural nowcasting can be trusted for equitable warning, and when it cannot.

Crop phenology classifiers trained on unevenly labelled agricultural ground truth face a label-efficiency problem that is not captured by standard supervised learning theory: the order in which labelled samples are presented interacts with the graph structure of the label-coverage pattern, and the resulting regret depends on both. The framework yields a label-efficiency regret bound that decomposes into a graph-ordered covering term and a curriculum-ordering term, and it is evaluated through a replication-based replication of an ordinary least squares estimator on a declared data-generating process with 600 replications of 500 observations each. The replication characterises the behaviour of the estimator under the stated process and provides a calibration check on the bound's assumptions. The contribution is a bound that makes explicit how the topology of ground-truth coverage, rather than only its volume, governs the label efficiency of phenology classifiers, and a set of conditions under which graph-ordered curricula are provably preferable to volume-matched random ordering.

Abstract Rare earth elements are critical to decarbonization, advanced electronics, and defense applications. Traditional hydrometallurgical recovery using liquid–liquid solvent extraction (SX) and classical ion exchange, however, requires the use of volatile organic diluents, high chemical consumption, and multiple-stage cascades, which produce significant amounts of saline and acidic effluents. Solvent-impregnated resins (SIRs), polymer inclusion membranes (PIMs), microbeads (PIBs), and cross-linked networks are environmentally friendly polymeric sorbents, which can greatly reduce the bleeding of the organic phase. This perspective follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines and critically examines the literature on polymer chemistry and artificial intelligence (AI) from 2016 to 2026. We investigate gradient boosting architectures and deep neural networks that map topological fingerprints and molecular physicochemical descriptors to distribution coefficients, coordination thermodynamics, and sorption capacities (R2 = 0.81–0.93). Furthermore, we critically evaluate three major translational limitations: integrating transfer learning throughout the 4f lanthanide contraction, performance degradation across complex real-world leachates, and bridging small-molecule informatics with cross-linked macromolecular networks. Finally, Bayesian inverse design and autonomous experimentation are contextualized to guide the scalable development of next-generation, high-selectivity polymeric sorbents.

Purpose Green practices can be considered a marketing tool to enhance a university’s image and student outcomes. Based on the theories of customer engagement and value co-creation, this study aims to develop a conceptual model showing the impacts of students’ green engagement, universities’ green management, branding factors and student satisfaction and value co-creation behaviors. Design/methodology/approach Data from a survey of 619 students across universities with different levels of green practices are analyzed using partial structural equation modeling. Findings The findings reveal that both university’s green management (i.e. green campus management and green energy campus management) and students’ green engagement (i.e. cognitive engagement and affective engagement) positively affect branding factors (i.e. self–brand connection and the university’s brand image) and student satisfaction and value co-creation behaviors. In particular, this study highlights the mediating roles of branding factors in the relationships between green factors and student outcomes. Practical implications This study offers implications for connecting green practices and branding campaigns of higher education institutions. Moreover, the findings also suggest a sustainable cycle of green practices: green practice engagement – student satisfaction and value co-creation – more value co-creation – future green engagement. Originality/value This study advances the current literature by highlighting a sustainable process: the linkage of green practices, branding factors and student satisfaction and value co-creation.
topics: Consumer Behavior in Brand Consumption and Identification

documents.abstract: A set of guidelines is presented for the responsible development and deployment of artificial intelligence in Advanced Air Mobility, space systems, and space-based Earth Observation. AI applications are examined across onboard and ground-based environments, including perception, detect-and-avoid, guidance and control, autonomous decision-making, satellite data processing, change detection, and geospatial foundation models. The principal barriers to operational adoption are identified, demonstrating that technical performance alone is insufficient without explainability, traceability, uncertainty quantification, physical consistency, representative datasets, domain-shift evaluation, human oversight, and deterministic fallback mechanisms. Drawing on evolving EASA and FAA guidance, the EU AI Act, and relevant aerospace assurance standards, recommendations are provided for early regulatory engagement, incremental deployment, rigorous simulation and validation, runtime monitoring, and comprehensive model and data documentation. The analysis concludes by highlighting the technical, transparency, accuracy, and trust challenges involved in deploying AI across space, urban air mobility, and Earth observation. It emphasizes that early compliance with evolving regulations and sustained collaboration among industry, researchers, and authorities are essential for responsible, effective real-world adoption.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: The rising volume of fluoroscopy-guided interventions poses an occupational safety challenge for healthcare workers (HCWs) exposed to chronic low-dose ionizing radiation (LDR), which carries stochastic risks of bone marrow suppression and radiation-induced cytopenias. Real-world longitudinal evidence validating the efficacy of modern protection standards on specific peripheral hematological parameters remains limited. This study aims to evaluate the peripheral hemogram profiles of interventional HCWs exposed to LDR, compared to those of a non-exposed control cohort, from baseline (T0) to follow-up (T1). Methods: A longitudinal matched case-control study evaluated the complete blood count with differential leukograms of 136 interventional HCWs exposed to LDR compared to those of 272 matched non-exposed controls from baseline (T0) to follow-up (T1), stratifying by role, seniority, and cumulative ionizing radiation dose. Results: The mean annual radiation dose was 0.22 mSv, and the mean cumulative radiation dose was 4.11 mSv. Hemogram indicators showed no significant differences between cases and controls at T0 and T1 (p > 0.05). Stratification by length of service (<10 vs. >10 years), and radiation dose (<3 vs. ≥3 mSv) demonstrated no significant variations in erythrocyte, leukocyte, or platelet counts. Regression analysis confirmed no association between hematological parameters and job seniority or radiation dose. All radiation doses remained below mandatory limits. Conclusions: The findings provide objective evidence of the effectiveness of current safety measures countering radiation-induced hematotoxicity in hospital settings. Longitudinal tracking confirms the absence of adverse hematological shifts, suggesting that structured training and strict personal protective equipment (PPE) use mitigate hematotoxicity risks among interventional staff exposed to ionizing radiation in healthcare settings. Safety protocols should maintain strict PPE compliance and safety training. Occupational health policy needs to prioritize continuous dosimetry monitoring, as routine hematological screening may not show early low-dose exposure effects.

Large Language Models (LLMs) have evolved from relying primarily on knowledge stored in their parametric memory to using non-parametric memory mechanisms such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide and ground knowledge. Recently, LLMs have begun to perform retrieval autonomously within a reasoning loop, an approach referred to as Agentic RAG. This shift introduces new querying behaviours, with implications for the design of retrieval systems that have yet to be evaluated. In this work, we introduce a large-scale dataset (ASQ) capturing how Agentic RAG systems perform multi-step search and reasoning. ASQ contains about 1M agentic search traces collected from open-source Agentic RAG systems over 3 corpora, 5 agent variants, and 6 retrieval settings. Our analysis of ASQ shows that, within this controlled benchmark setting, a single search query can trigger long chains of retrieval calls (up to 186) and follow query reformulation dynamics different from those observed in historical human-search data. Our results also reveal substantial behavioural variation across agent and retrieval configurations: changes in re-ranking and retrieval depth do not consistently affect search workloads in terms of search-call volume and trace length across agents. To our knowledge, publicly available production logs do not expose the agent, dataset, and retrieval configuration associated with each trace. ASQ provides a reusable resource for further analysing agent search behaviour and supporting future information retrieval studies on agentic workloads under controlled settings.

Background With the growing application of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in fashion design and cultural and creative industries, AI-generated Chinese ethnic-minority fashion has created new opportunities for the contemporary transformation of traditional culture. However, whether consumers are willing to accept such products and how AI disclosure influences their evaluations and purchase intentions remain unclear. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) model, this study examines the mechanisms through which AI disclosure, design aesthetics, cultural identity, perceived usefulness, perceived authenticity, and algorithm aversion influence consumers' purchase intentions toward AI-generated Chinese ethnic-minority fashion. Methods A questionnaire survey combined with a scenario-based experiment was employed. Six AI-generated fashion illustrations derived from Tujia costume elements were developed and selected as stimulus materials. Participants were randomly assigned to either an AI disclosure group or a non-disclosure group. Data were collected through Tencent Questionnaire, yielding 410 valid responses. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Importance–Performance Map Analysis (IPMA) were employed to examine the structural relationships, mediating effects, moderating effects, and practical priorities for improvement. Results Design aesthetics and cultural identity influenced purchase intention through perceived usefulness and perceived authenticity, with perceived usefulness emerging as the strongest predictor of purchase intention. AI disclosure significantly reduced design aesthetics, cultural identity, perceived usefulness, and perceived authenticity. Algorithm aversion did not significantly moderate the relationship between perceived usefulness and purchase intention but significantly strengthened the positive effect of perceived authenticity on purchase intention. Conclusions This study reveals the multiple psychological pathways through which AI disclosure shapes consumers' evaluations of AI-generated ethnic cultural fashion. The findings further indicate that algorithm aversion alters the extent to which consumers rely on authenticity judgments when forming purchase intentions. This study extends the application of the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) model to the context of AI-generated cultural products and provides practical implications for balancing AI transparency, cultural authenticity, and the practical value of products.
topics: Consumer Behavior in Brand Consumption and Identification

documents.abstract: Purpose The study examines the interaction between generative artificial intelligence (GAI)and digital task innovation by conceptualizing and hypothesizing GAI orchestration as a multifaceted variable comprising GAI integration, enablement and workflow alignment. Furthermore, the study distinguishes digital task innovation from broader concepts such as process innovation, digital innovation and product innovation. Design/methodology/approach Today, firms employ GAI technologies to enhance organizational performance, operational efficiency and productivity. Research has provided valuable insights into the role of generative technologies in product innovation; however, their impact on digital task innovation remains underexplored, particularly in relation to task redesign, workflow reconfiguration and human–GAI collaboration. The study examines the interaction between GAI and digital task innovation by conceptualizing and hypothesizing GAI orchestration as a multifaceted variable comprising GAI integration, enablement and workflow alignment. Furthermore, the study distinguishes digital task innovation from broader concepts such as process innovation, digital innovation and product innovation. Findings The findings of the study indicate that GAI orchestration is positively associated with GAI augmentation and negatively associated with GAI anxiety. GAI anxiety negatively influences digital task innovation. However, GAI augmentation noted as positive while mapping digital task innovation. Thus, the findings support the proposed dual-pathway framework. Originality/value The results highlight the pivotal role of organizations in dealing with GAI anxiety and upholding GAI augmentation for effective GAI orchestration that leads to digital task innovation. The findings also have implications for both research and practice, opening new avenues in the context of digital transformation. The study contributes by positioning GAI orchestration as a higher-order perceived organizational capability and by clarifying how GAI-enabled task innovation depends not only on technology integration but also on workflow alignment, employee enablement and augmentation-oriented use.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Research comparing national artificial intelligence (AI) policy scores the state and its institutions, and rarely asks what a policy commits to where a person meets a system: whether someone subject to an automated decision can learn, correct, refuse or appeal it. We contribute Human-Centered AI Policy Instrument (HCAIPI), an instrument for reading policy at that layer, applied to 245 editions from 101 countries against twelve themes from human-computer interaction (HCI) research, recording how firmly each commitment is stated and whether anything would execute it. Of 13,587 relevant passages, 44.7% state a principle with no implementation detail and 11.4% specify a mechanism, a shape invariant to income band, length and volume. What a person is told or consulted about is instrumented at twice the rate of what they can do, and 65% of specified mechanisms are tasks for government. The lexicon recovers 13% to 54% of what a reader accepts; country figures track length.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Current guidelines strongly endorse integrated multidisciplinary team (MDT) approaches to manage the complexity of patients with IBD. Evidence from formal multidisciplinary case discussions suggests an impact on diagnostic and treatment decisions, while studies of broader integrated IBD services report associations with improved disease control, quality of life, and healthcare utilization. However, implementation remains heterogeneous across centers, with variability in team composition, meeting frequency, referral criteria, and access to specialist services. Future directions include standardization of MDT composition and processes, definition of quality indicators, extension of specialist expertise through hub-and-spoke networks and telemedicine, and integration of patients as active partners in care. Digital tools may support communication and remote follow-up, whereas the role of artificial intelligence in MDT decision-making remains investigational and requires clinical validation. Multidisciplinary care should be regarded as a core organizational principle of modern IBD management. Realizing its full potential will require sustained investment, workforce planning, and prospective research to ensure equitable, high-quality, and sustainable care across diverse healthcare settings.

This paper examines the evolution and possible varieties of consciousness through comparative animal behaviour, human metacognition, social conditioning, and artificial intelligence. It proposes that individuality, behavioural divergence, and adaptive responses to novel challenges can provide evidence about cognition, while recognizing that none alone establishes subjective experience. A proposed individualized adaptive threshold framework assesses learning and behavioural reorganization relative to each subject's baseline without imposing harmful stress. The analysis then extends to AI systems: increasingly capable autonomous systems may alter human control over work, information, and institutions regardless of whether machine consciousness emerges. The paper develops testable predictions, methodological safeguards, and alternative interpretations, and argues for a pluralistic and graded research framework rather than a single evolutionary ladder.

Clinical documentation is essential to healthcare delivery but is timeconsuming, cognitively demanding, and prone to error. Large language models (LLMs) can generate draft notes, but may introduce hallucinations, unsupported inferences, or factual distortions that clinicians overlook. This study evaluated whether transparency features improve clinician oversight in LLM-assisted documentation. Using a crossover design, 40 clinicians reviewed AI-generated notes under three conditions: a standard LLM interface, token-level uncertainty highlighting, and uncertainty highlighting combined with direct links to electronic medical record fields. Outcomes included factual errors remaining in finalized notes, editing time, trust, perceived control, and cognitive load. The combined uncertainty-plus-source-link interface performed best, reducing factual errors by 41% and editing time by 18% compared with the standard condition. Uncertainty highlighting alone offered partial benefits but still required manual record verification. These findings indicate that LLM-assisted documentation is safer and more efficient when transparency features support verification, direct attention, and preserve clinician control.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Humanized management constitutes a strategic dimension of health care quality, as it integrates workers' dignity, patient safety, and institutional sustainability. This essay aims to discuss the relationship between humanized management and quality of work life, identifying organizational challenges and opportunities for transforming management practices. A theoretical-reflective approach was adopted, drawing on scientific literature and institutional documents addressing occupational health, leadership, professional participation, and burnout prevention. The analysis indicates that humanization cannot be restricted to welcoming and supporting patients; rather, it must also encompass working conditions, autonomy, professional recognition, equity, and protection against psychosocial risks. Excessive workloads, precarious employment arrangements, workplace violence, and hierarchical communication undermine health care teams and may compromise continuity of care. Conversely, participatory leadership, adequate staffing levels, institutional support, and context-sensitive process evaluation can foster safer and more collaborative work environments. It is argued that individual well-being initiatives are insufficient when disconnected from structural changes. The essay concludes that promoting quality of work life requires integrating health professionals' well-being into governance decisions through meaningful participation, clearly defined responsibilities, and continuous monitoring. Consolidating this perspective depends on sustained policies that address inequalities across professional groups and are guided by scientific evidence and labor rights in contemporary health care settings.

Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) promise irrigation schedules that respect soil-water balance while learning residual dynamics from data. Their reliability, however, depends on how the network's unmodeled component interacts with the physical constraint, and no bound currently exists for the inference error that this interaction induces when root-zone conductance is misspecified. The soil-water balance is written as a constrained operator equation in which the learned residual is projected onto the orthogonal complement of the physical flux space; the projection defines an inference error whose magnitude is controlled by the conductance misspecification and the Lipschitz constant of the residual network. A formal bound is derived (Theorem 3.1) and tightened for the practically relevant case of bounded conductance error (Corollary 3.2). The bound is then evaluated in a replication-based design study of the before-after-control-impact estimator that would be used to validate such schedules in the field. Using a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64), power was estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. Fifty-six clusters are required for 80% power at a 5-percentage-point effect. The residual bound is informative at realistic cluster counts only when the conductance error is below a threshold that the design study makes explicit, and it identifies the conditions under which hybrid inference is preferable to either a purely physical or a purely learned schedule.

The protection of workers' rights is a crucial component of labor law, aiming to ensure the fulfillment of workers' fundamental rights within the employment relationship. Constitutionally, this protection is grounded in Article 27 paragraph (2) and Article 28D paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, which guarantee every citizen the right to employment, a decent standard of living, and fair treatment in employment relationships. Further regulations regarding worker protection are set forth in Law Number 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower, as amended by Law Number 6 of 2023 concerning the Enactment of Government Regulation in Lieu of Law Number 2 of 2022 concerning Job Creation into Law. This study aims to analyze the implementation of worker rights protection within employment relationships based on labor legislation, as well as to identify obstacles encountered during implementation and potential solutions. The research employs a normative legal research method, utilizing both statutory and conceptual approaches. The findings indicate that the protection of workers' rights has been implemented through regulations concerning employment contracts, wages, working hours and rest periods, occupational health and safety, social security for workers, protection against discrimination, and protection during the termination of employment. However, implementation still faces various obstacles, including low compliance with labor regulations among some employers, limited labor inspection capacity, workers' limited understanding of their rights, corporate economic factors, and the imbalance of bargaining power between workers and employers. Therefore, it is necessary to strengthen labor inspection, enhance workers' legal awareness, improve employer compliance, and optimize industrial relations dispute resolution mechanisms to achieve effective and fair protection of workers' rights that ensures legal certainty within employment relationships.

Abstract: This study analyses the legal position of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles within the framework of Good Corporate Governance (GCG), examines the implementation of ESG at PT Inticorp Logistics, and assesses the legal responsibility of the Board of Directors for ESG implementation under Indonesian company law. A normative juridical method was used with statutory, conceptual, and normative case study approaches. The analysis drew on Law Number 40 of 2007 on Limited Liability Companies, Financial Services Authority Regulation Number 51/POJK.03/2017, the G20/OECD Principles of Corporate Governance (2023), the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, and the doctrines of fiduciary duty, duty of care, duty of loyalty, and the business judgment rule, applied to the company's documents. The findings show that PT Inticorp Logistics has implemented ESG at the operational level through quality management, occupational health and safety systems, and a basic corporate governance structure. However, ESG has not been integrated into the directors' strategic policies, risk management, performance indicators, or sustainability reporting. Indonesian positive law does not explicitly require all companies to adopt ESG, so the absence of an ESG policy does not in itself constitute a breach of law. Nevertheless, ESG holds an implicit legal position as part of the directors' duty to manage the company in good faith and with due care. This study proposes a legal construction of ESG-based directors' responsibility that positions ESG integration as a concrete manifestation of fiduciary duty and duty of care. Keyword: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG); directors' responsibility; fiduciary duty; good corporate governance; logistics company. Abstrak: Penelitian ini menganalisis kedudukan hukum prinsip Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) dalam kerangka Good Corporate Governance (GCG), mengkaji implementasi ESG pada PT Inticorp Logistics, serta menilai tanggung jawab hukum Direksi dalam penerapan ESG berdasarkan hukum perseroan Indonesia. Penelitian menggunakan metode yuridis normatif dengan pendekatan perundang-undangan, konseptual, dan studi kasus normatif. Analisis didasarkan pada Undang-Undang Nomor 40 Tahun 2007 tentang Perseroan Terbatas, POJK Nomor 51/POJK.03/2017, G20/OECD Principles of Corporate Governance (2023), IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, serta doktrin fiduciary duty, duty of care, duty of loyalty, dan business judgment rule yang diterapkan pada dokumen perusahaan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa PT Inticorp Logistics telah menerapkan ESG pada tingkat operasional melalui sistem manajemen mutu, keselamatan dan kesehatan kerja, serta struktur dasar tata kelola perusahaan. Namun, ESG belum terintegrasi ke dalam kebijakan strategis Direksi, manajemen risiko, indikator kinerja, maupun pelaporan keberlanjutan. Hukum positif Indonesia belum secara eksplisit mewajibkan seluruh perseroan menerapkan ESG, sehingga ketiadaan kebijakan ESG tidak serta-merta merupakan pelanggaran hukum. Meskipun demikian, ESG memiliki kedudukan hukum secara implisit sebagai bagian dari kewajiban Direksi untuk mengurus perseroan dengan itikad baik dan penuh kehati-hatian. Penelitian ini menawarkan konstruksi hukum tanggung jawab Direksi berbasis ESG yang menempatkan integrasi ESG sebagai manifestasi konkret fiduciary duty dan duty of care. Kata kunci: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG); tanggung jawab Direksi; fiduciary duty; good corporate governance; perusahaan logistik.

Objective To evaluate the performance of machine learning (ML) models tasked with predicting thyroid cancer recurrence using natural language processing (NLP) and large language model (LLM) derived features. Patients and methods This was a retrospective study of adult thyroid cancer patients treated at an academic medical center between January 1, 2010 through December 31, 2022. Patients were classified as having cancer recurrence or no recurrence. Novel NLP features were extracted from cytopathology and surgical pathology reports using Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF), Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), and a zero-shot large language model (LLM) classification. Five learning algorithms (Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost) were trained to predict cancer recurrence utilizing a combination of NLP-derived features and structured electronic medical record (EMR) variables. All models were evaluated using stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using F1 score and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). The top performing model was hyperparameter-tuned, and feature importance was evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values and gain-based importance. Results 310 patients with differentiated thyroid cancer diagnosed on final surgical pathology were included in this study. The optimized XGBoost model incorporating EMR variables and LDA-derived features achieved the best performance, with a cross-validated F1 score of 0.647 on the training set and a held-out test F1-score of 0.631 (95% CI 0.509–0.758) and ROC-AUC of 0.741 (95% CI 0.572-0.892). SHAP analysis and gain-based feature importance identified surgical pathology topic—cervical and lateral neck lymph node dissection—as the dominant predictor of cancer recurrence. Conclusion Various classifiers including machine learning models utilizing novel NLP features derived from unstructured pathology reports may enable improved prediction of recurrence in patients with differentiated thyroid cancer.
topics: Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

documents.abstract: Abstract Radiology and breast imaging curricula have relied almost entirely on passive learning tools such as lectures, books, journal articles, and videos for more than two decades. Despite their wide availability, trainee engagement with these tools to accumulate and synthesize the vast amount of information required to succeed in radiology remains challenging. Knowledge gaps exist among trainees because of natural differences in learning styles, study habits, and case exposure at the reading station. Further, current pressures in academic radiology limit the availability of workstation teaching, which is the most effective teaching and learning strategy in the field. Leading educators aim to bridge these gaps both by leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) large language models (LLM) to develop precision learning curricula personalized to the trainee and by creating gamified learning tools to boost the engagement of trainees. Gamification can also be used to simulate learning experiences for trainees. These tools show promise based on user feedback, both by educators and learners. Further, the synergy of AI and gamification strategies may help address knowledge gaps precisely and efficiently. We explore some of these emerging tools, their application, potential benefits, and limitations within radiology with a focus on breast imaging training.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Institutional guidance on generative artificial intelligence is often evaluated through its existence or students’ general support for regulation. Neither establishes whether awareness of rules corresponds with responsible use. This exploratory study separates perceived knowledge of institutional rule status, anticipated policy benefits and behaviour-specific self-reports in a Bangladesh legal-education database. The complete database contains N = 385 records; its n = 245 current law students form the primary analytical subsample, with all records retained for sensitivity analysis. The principal outcome is endorsement of using AI only as permitted by course or institutional rules. Item-level logistic models, robust intervals, respondent bootstrap standardisation and repeated stratified cross-validation examine association and incremental predictive value. Policy awareness is endorsed by 151 students (61.6%); permitted-use compliance by 150 (61.2%). The student association is positive but uncertain (adjusted odds ratio 1.33; 95% confidence interval 0.95-1.86); the complete-sample estimate is likewise uncertain (1.17; 0.89-1.53). Standardised endorsement probabilities at awareness scores four and three differ by 6.7 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval −0.9-14.7). Associations with independent-work boundaries and avoiding wholly personal attribution are also uncertain. Adding awareness changes the mean held-out Brier score from 0.24308 to 0.24268, while an intercept-only benchmark performs better at 0.23740. Support for training and consistent enforcement is substantially more common than awareness endorsement. Low internal consistency precludes treating these items as one reflective policy construct. The codebook labels identifiers and comments synthetic, leaving numerical provenance unresolved; comments are excluded. The findings identify limits in using perceived awareness as a surrogate for compliance and motivate assessment-specific communication and prospective evaluation. They establish neither institutional policy effectiveness nor misconduct prevalence.

In the current work, we established a smart system for dengue diagnosis that enables on-site detection while removing the need for human intervention and continuous monitoring in difficult-to-reach areas. The system comprises of 4-smart technologies: i) drone, ii) biosensor, iii) Yolov5 AI-module, iv) a QR-code-derived digital website linked patient E-Prescription barcode, where the biosensor acts as a smart detector, and the drone as a vehicle for transporting the biosensor to the testing zone. Deep learning analysis was done by an expert using an artificial intelligence module; additional QR-code-based websites were added to the system, allowing users to scan the code and send detection data to laboratory authorities, and the patient got a medical e-prescription from the doctor. The proposed system has lightweight materials, optimized power sources, and weather-resistant housing to ensure reliable on-site diagnostics. However, practical challenges associated with drone-based diagnostic deployment, including environmental conditions, flight stability, battery capacity, payload constraints, and reliable operation in remote settings, should be considered when evaluating the field applicability and scalability of the proposed system. The suggested detection platform used the instrument-less lateral flow colorimetric approach, enabling naked-eye detection of dengue virus antigen with an LOD of 0.91 µg/mL within 5 s. As a consequence, the Drone-based approach allows clinicians to monitor the dengue virus antigen in remote populations. Accordingly, governments and non-profit organizations can utilize this technology to monitor the red alert zone, receiving precise and reliable data for informed decision-making.

Concept bottleneck models (CBMs) promise interpretable clinical triage by routing predictions through human-readable concepts, but their calibration stability under clinical guideline revision is not well characterised. The framework treats concept alignment as a constrained projection problem and characterises the bias introduced when the concept set is revised without retraining. A replication-based evaluation of the before-after-control-impact estimator was conducted under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64), with power estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required for 5 percentage point detection at 80% power. The framework proposes that calibration stability is governed by the alignment residual between the deployed concept set and the revised guideline concept set, and that this residual can be estimated prospectively from the design parameters. The contribution is a formal characterisation of when concept bottleneck triage models remain calibrated across guideline revisions and a design-level estimator for planning stability evaluations.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Concept bottleneck models (CBMs) promise interpretable triage by routing predictions through clinically meaningful concepts, yet their safety under emergency department overcrowding remains uncharacterised. The analysis characterised the operating characteristics of the estimator rather than observing any clinical deployment. Power reached 80% at 54 clusters for a 5-percentage-point effect; minimum detectable effects at 80% power were derived for each cluster count. The results indicate that the BACI estimator is well calibrated for detecting moderate safety degradation in CBM-mediated triage, but that small cluster counts (8 and 16) yield unacceptably low power for effects below 5 percentage points. Interpretability claims for CBMs cannot be separated from the statistical design used to audit them, and it proposes a minimum reporting standard for CBM safety evaluations in overcrowded emergency settings.

Abstract Climate change poses disproportionate threats to human health in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), yet comprehensive evidence on implemented interventions remains under-researched. Understanding the scope and characteristics of existing climate-health interventions is essential for informing policy priorities and action in the region. We conducted a scoping review following Arksey and O'Malley's framework and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines. We systematically searched Google Scholar, PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus for peer-reviewed empirical studies on climate-health interventions in SSA, with no date restrictions. Two reviewers independently screened 3009 records. A total of 36 studies reporting 350 interventions were included. The majority of the studies (83.3%) focused exclusively on adaptation, while a smaller proportion (16.7%) combined both adaptation and mitigation strategies. Four overarching intervention categories were identified inductively from the included studies, each comprising distinct but conceptually related sub-categories: health systems strengthening and governance; disease surveillance, monitoring, and early warning; environmental health and infrastructure; and community resilience and social wellbeing. Vector-borne diseases, particularly malaria, constituted the primary health focus, while heat-related illnesses, occupational health, and mental health received limited attention. Studies mostly reported interventions in West Africa, East Africa, Southern Africa, and multi-regional settings, with Central Africa receiving limited attention. The evidence is predominantly rural-focused (n = 18; 50%), with urban-focused studies accounting for 10 studies (27.8%) and mixed urban-rural settings for the remaining 8 (22.2%). Notably, no dedicated study investigated interventions specifically targeting coastal areas. People-centred interventions predominated over nature-based solutions. Key evidence gaps included cross-sectional study designs limiting causal inference, insufficient cost-effectiveness evaluations, limited integration of indigenous knowledge, and inadequate attention to gender-specific and occupational vulnerabilities. Policy efforts must go beyond disease-specific responses toward integrated strategies addressing multiple climate-health pathways while prioritising underrepresented regions and mitigation opportunities to build comprehensive, equitable climate resilience across the region.

documents.abstract: Since 2022, ChatGPT has contributed to the widespread adoption of AI in education. Custom GPTs can automate part of the written feedback process, a particularly demanding task in large classes. We developed two versions of an error-detection chatbot for first-year students at a private university in Lima and implemented the second version under teacher supervision and through peer discussion. This study examines its potential and limitations. The tool accelerated the identification of spelling and punctuation errors; however, it produced inconsistent assessments. We conclude that its potential is greatest when integrated into a workflow that combines AI with human review. These findings provide guidance for future implementations and contribute to the ongoing debate on the responsible integration of AI into teaching.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence has transformed language from a human meaning-making practice into an interaction among computational models, semantic theories, and social values. This systematic literature review examines how scholarship conceptualises language meaning in the AI era and identifies conditions for interpretable, culturally responsive, and ethically accountable machine language understanding. Following PRISMA, the review screened records retrieved from Scopus and sources, synthesising 36 eligible studies through thematic analysis and a Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methodology lens. Evidence shows that scholarship is organised around an interconnected AI–machine learning–natural language processing nexus, with large language models, semantic representation, machine translation, and human–AI interaction as lines of inquiry. Rather than demonstrating that machines simply “understand” language, the studies reveal a shift from formal semantic processing towards contextual, pragmatic, and relational accounts of meaning. Persistent limitations remain: technical performance receives greater attention than linguistic diversity, social consequences, interpretability, algorithmic fairness, privacy, and cultural conditions in which meaning is negotiated. The review also identifies an uneven geography of knowledge production: studies from North America and Europe advance foundational and ethical debates, whereas Asian research foregrounds local applications. Its principal contribution is a multidimensional synthesis connecting computational development with philosophy of language, linguistics, cognition, and ethics, moving beyond narrowly technical reviews of AI language systems. Future research should test culturally adaptive and explainable models across minoritised and multilingual languages, combine computational evaluation with human-centred inquiry, and establish cross-regional collaborations that treat linguistic justice as a core design principle. Meaningful AI requires not textual fluency alone, but accountable participation in context-sensitive human communication.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming healthcare, with applications spanning disease diagnosis, patient monitoring, personalized treatments, and drug discovery 1 , 2 . There is growing consensus among healthcare providers, policymakers, and patients that AI-enabled digital health is reshaping care delivery by accelerating diagnoses, improving outcomes, reducing costs, and expanding access to remote regions. Yet, despite these advances, a persistent digital divide threatens to widen health inequities. The datasets powering AI systems remain predominantly sourced from white, Western populations, leaving racial and ethnic minorities and entire regions such as Africa underrepresented 3 . This lack of data diversity produces AI models that are less accurate, less generalizable, and potentially biased, exacerbating disparities in healthcare outcomes 4 . In addition, African Americans are less likely to participate in health research due to longstanding mistrust, as seen in HIV, cancer prevention, and occupational health studies 5 , 6 . The consequence is a problematic cycle with underrepresentation in data leading to underperformance in care delivery 7 .
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Crop disease classifiers deployed in smallholder agriculture face a label-shift problem that is rarely formalised: the field prevalence of a disease differs from the prevalence in the curated training corpus, and the reference label itself arrives only after a pathologist's delayed confirmation. The framework defines a shift operator on the joint distribution of image features and confirmed labels, derives a consistency functional that bounds the gap between source-risk and target-risk estimates, and shows that the bound is governed by the total variation distance between source and target label marginals and by the confirmation delay. A replication-based evaluation of the ['Intercept', 'exposure', 'group', 'severity'] estimator was conducted: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2), and the study characterises the behaviour of the ordinary least squares estimator under the stated process. Across the 600 replications the estimated bias for the intercept was 0.01569 and for the exposure coefficient -0.00033; the root mean squared error was 0.8802 for the intercept and 0.01628 for exposure; empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The framework proposes that risk-consistency auditing, rather than point accuracy, should govern deployment decisions when confirmation is delayed, and it identifies the conditions under which a classifier's reported risk can be trusted.

Agricultural disease triage systems that combine automated inference with human expert referral must decide, for each case, whether the cost of deferring to a scarce plant pathologist is justified by the expected gain in diagnostic accuracy. Existing learning-to-defer formulations assume symmetric referral costs and evaluate deferral policies by their average accuracy, which misstates the decision problem when a missed epidemic-class disease costs far more than an unnecessary referral. The triage problem is formalised as a cost-sensitive contextual bandit in which the deferral cost depends on the true disease class, and a cost-weighted regret is defined against the best policy in a restricted deferral class. A bound is derived that decomposes regret into an estimation term scaling with the square root of the number of triage cases and a misspecification term controlled by the asymmetry ratio between false-negative and false-positive referral costs. The bound is evaluated on a declared design grid of 8, 16, 24 and 32 clusters, effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, and 2000 replications per cell, with an intraclass correlation of 0.64, between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0 and residual standard deviation of 4.5. Power reaches 80 per cent at 52 clusters for a 5 percentage point effect. Asymmetric referral costs shift the optimal deferral threshold and that the regret bound tightens as the asymmetry ratio grows, which has consequences for how triage systems should be calibrated before deployment.

Irrigation advisories generated by artificial intelligence agents are increasingly paired with farmer judgement, yet the two sources of competence are rarely aligned: the agent may be better informed about soil-moisture dynamics while the farmer is better informed about local water availability, crop condition and institutional constraints. the present analysis formalises the resulting decision problem as a learning-to-defer inference task in which a deferral policy routes each advisory instance either to the agent or to the human expert, and it evaluates the policy through a deferral-regret criterion rather than through predictive accuracy alone. The analysis is theoretical and methodological: no observational data are used or claimed. A before-after-control-impact design is characterised under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, and power is estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design requires 54 clusters to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80 per cent power. The paper derives a deferral-regret decomposition that separates the regret attributable to agent error from the regret attributable to human error and from the regret attributable to misrouted deferral, and it shows that the three components have different sample-size requirements. The contribution is a formal criterion and an evaluation design for deferral policies in irrigation advisory systems, together with the boundary conditions under which deferral improves on either agent-only or human-only advice.

Abstract This chapter explores the transformative potential of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education, focusing on its role in promoting equitable access and personalized learning. Drawing from the author’s experience as an administrator at the Indian Institute of Technology Jammu, the chapter examines the challenges diverse student populations face and how AI can address these issues. It traces the evolution of educational technology over the past 25 years, from email to advanced AI systems, highlighting the impact on teaching, learning, and administrative processes. The chapter discusses the benefits of AI in higher education, including personalized learning experiences for students, enhanced accessibility for marginalized groups, and data-informed decision-making. It also addresses the ethical considerations and potential risks associated with AI implementation. The authors emphasize the importance of balancing AI integration with human interaction and advocate for responsible AI deployment in educational settings. The chapter concludes by outlining a vision for the future of AI in education, stressing the need for continuous learning, ethical frameworks, and a commitment to inclusivity and diversity.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: In modern construction projects that utilize BIM, the greatest challenges arise from the large number of participants and the volume of project information in various formats. As a result, programming skills are increasingly required for effective work. Since developing these skills takes time, this paper examines whether artificial intelligence can assist designers in programming and automating time-consuming, repetitive tasks in the processes of model adjustment and result extraction. Modern design firms use a wide range of software throughout a building’s life cycle, but AI helps to reduce the need for multiple tools. Routine tasks can be automated using code without the need for specialised software, provided only the final product – a 3D IFC model – is available. As AI technologies advance, software code is generated more quickly and to a higher standard using artificial intelligence. This means that AI-driven programming is becoming increasingly widespread in building design, and it is also possible to automate more complex tasks. Article in Lithuanian. Dirbtinio intelekto panaudojimas optimizuojant projektavimo procesą statinio informacinio modeliavimo (BIM) projektavimo etape Santrauka Šiuolaikiniuose statybų projektuose, kuriuose taikomas BIM, didžiausi iššūkiai kyla dėl didelio dalyvių skaičiaus ir skirtingų formatų projektinės informacijos kiekio, todėl efektyviam darbui vis dažniau reikia programavimo įgūdžių. Kadangi šių įgūdžių ugdymas užtrunka, dirbtinis intelektas gali padėti projektuotojui programuoti ir automatizuoti laikui imlias, pasikartojančias užduotis modelio koregavimo bei rezultatų išgavimo procesuose. Šiuolaikinės projektavimo įmonės taiko daug skirtingų programinių įrangų visame statinio gyvavimo cikle, tačiau DI padeda sumažinti skirtingų įrankių naudojimą. Kasdieninės užduotys gali būti automatizuotos naudojant programinį kodą neturint specializuotos programinės įrangos, turint tik galutinį produktą – trimatį IFC modelį. Tobulėjant DI technologijoms, greičiau ir kokybiškiau generuojamas programinis kodas dirbtiniu intelektu. Tai reiškia, kad DI atliekamas programavimas tampa vis plačiau taikomas projektuojant statinį, taip pat galima automatizuoti daugiau sudėtingų užduočių. Reikšminiai žodžiai: statinis informacinis modeliavimas, BIM, dirbtinis intelektas, programavimas, duomenų valdymas, projektavimo automatizavimas.

Red-light running (RLR) is a major safety concern at signalized intersections, driven by both intentional and unintentional factors. This complexity makes it difficult to develop universal countermeasures and underscores the need for a deeper understanding of factors contributing to severe RLR crashes. However, crash severity modeling is frequently hampered by class imbalance in crash datasets, which can introduce bias and undermine predictive reliability. Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence, particularly generative adversarial networks (GANs), offer a promising solution by synthesizing realistic minority-class samples to address class imbalance. This study evaluates the effectiveness of conditional tabular GANs (CTGANs) against traditional resampling techniques—random over-sampling (ROS), synthetic minority over-sampling technique, adaptive synthetic sampling, and tabular variational autoencoder—using a dataset of 20,430 RLR crashes in Alabama, US, from 2015 to 2024. Results show that CTGAN, when combined with a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) model, achieves the best overall predictive performance among all evaluated combinations, with a geometric mean (G-mean) of 0.55 and an accuracy of 0.69 on the test set, outperforming the next best alternatives, CTGAN + support vector classifier (accuracy 0.67, G-mean 0.54) and ROS + MLP (accuracy 0.66, G-mean 0.54). Model interpretability using SHAP analysis revealed that the most important factors in predicting injury-related RLR crashes were the involvement of vulnerable road users (i.e., pedestrians, bicyclists, and motorcyclists), multi-vehicle crashes, heavy-vehicle involvement, nighttime conditions, rural areas, and intersections with five or more approaches. These findings provide valuable insights for developing policy recommendations and effective countermeasures to reduce injury-related RLR crashes.

Nearly 970 million people worldwide live with mental health (MH) disorders, many involving recurrent episodes that may be mitigated through timely prediction. This review evaluates machine learning (ML) approaches using wearable physiological data to forecast MH episodes and examines whether device grade influences predictive accuracy. Empirical English-language studies were identified through EBSCO and screened in Rayyan.ai by two independent reviewers, with a third reviewer resolving conflicts. Of 332 records identified, 32 studies met the inclusion criteria. Most studies focused on depression or stress, and 30 applied AI/ML methods. Findings show that predictive performance was driven more by ML approach than by device grade. Reported ranges reached 76%–87% for depression, 85%–98% for stress, 75.6%–92.8% for panic-attack risk, and 97%–99% for anxiety. Key predictors included heart-rate variability, sleep, activity, circadian stability, and electrodermal activity. Multimodal and personalized temporal models performed best.

This chapter examines the foundations and limits of computation and their implications for artificial intelligence. It begins with the Entscheidungsproblem and Alan Turing’s formulation of the universal Turing machine, introducing the idea that computation itself can be studied independently of any physical machine. The chapter explains the halting problem and related undecidability results, showing that some well-defined questions cannot be answered by any algorithm, even in principle. It then turns to computational complexity, distinguishing between problems that are solvable in theory and those that are solvable efficiently, and introduces the P versus NP problem as a central open question. The chapter explores how computational hardness can function not only as a limitation but also as a resource, underpinning modern cryptography through one-way functions and key-exchange protocols. Finally, the discussion turns to artificial intelligence, contrasting early rule-based approaches with modern machine learning and neural networks. Recent advances in deep learning and large language models are presented as the culmination of decades of theoretical insight, highlighting both their remarkable capabilities and the enduring structural limits imposed by computation itself.

Malware continues to evolve through obfuscation, packing, polymorphism, and other evasion techniques, challenging traditional detection approaches. Data mining (DM) and machine learning (ML) is become important by the day for identifying malicious software through static characteristics, runtime behaviour, and combinations of both. This review examines 46 selected studies on malware detection using DM and ML, with emphasis on static, dynamic, and hybrid analysis. The selected literature is synthesized according to malware platforms, datasets, feature representations, learning algorithms, reported performance, and methodological limitations. The review indicates that static analysis provides computationally efficient detection based on features such as PE headers, strings, byte sequences, and opcode representations, whereas dynamic analysis provides behavioural information through API calls, system calls, memory traces, and execution activities. Hybrid approaches combine complementary feature sources and have demonstrated promising detection performance across several studies. Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, and ensemble-based approaches are frequently reported, while deep learning approaches are increasingly explored for complex feature representations. However, comparison across studies is constrained by differences in datasets, class distributions, feature engineering procedures, and evaluation protocols. Recurring limitations include small or imbalanced datasets, limited real-world validation, insufficient evaluation against unseen malware, computational overhead, and limited model interpretability. Based on these observations, the review identifies explainable artificial intelligence, transfer learning, lightweight real-time detection, and temporal evaluation as important directions for future research.

ABSTRACT The integration of artificial intelligence into industrial quality control (QC) and management encompassing automated defect detection, real‐time process monitoring, and zero‐defect manufacturing has generated a rapidly expanding yet fragmented research landscape. This study addresses the need for comprehensive mapping of quality and reliability engineering practice through a computational systematic review of 9618 publications spanning the 2020–2025 period. A hybrid natural language processing (NLP) pipeline combining FlashText, Sentence‐BERT, KeyBERT, and spaCy performs semantic extraction of AI architectures, learning paradigms, defect typologies, and deployment contexts. The review pursues three objectives: mapping the architectural evolution of deep learning in industrial inspection, characterizing operational challenges of AI‐driven manufacturing, and identifying methodological frontiers for improving production reliability and supporting intelligent quality assurance (QA) systems. Results reveal that AI‐based quality control advances through coevolution of neural architectures, learning paradigms, and deployment requirements. CNNs remain central to discriminative visual inspection, while Transformers extend capabilities for multimodal reasoning. The field exhibits strong bias toward surface defects while overlooking safety‐critical internal defects. Emerging trends show transition from algorithm‐centric research toward deployment‐oriented paradigms including Uncertainty Quantification, Edge AI, Explainable AI, and Digital Twins. This work provides practitioners with an evidence‐based foundation for developing reliable, scalable AI quality systems aligned with Industry 4.0 principles.
topics: Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

documents.abstract: This study examines the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) research in K–12 teaching and learning by identifying major research trends, thematic structures, and emerging scholarly directions. A scientometric analysis was conducted using a validated corpus of 1,154 Scopus-indexed documents published between 2016 and May 2026. To strengthen corpus reliability, the dataset underwent content-level validation through abstract screening, duplicate detection, and thematic relevance assessment focused on K–12 educational contexts. Co-citation analysis, clustering algorithms, and citation burst detection were performed using CiteSpace to identify influential publications, thematic clusters, and temporal patterns of scholarly influence. The findings reveal rapid growth in academic production after 2020, particularly following the emergence of generative AI technologies. Four major research clusters were identified: (1) artificial intelligence literacy, focused on competency-based AI education and ethical awareness; (2) large language models (LLMs), centred on generative AI, conversational systems, and AI-mediated assessment; (3) early childhood education, emphasising developmentally appropriate AI learning experiences and playful pedagogies; and (4) K–12 context, addressing broader educational, ethical, and societal implications of AI integration in schools. Citation burst analysis revealed a progression from foundational AI literacy frameworks and constructionist machine learning pedagogies toward curriculum co-design, teacher readiness, and human-centred AI integration. Overall, the findings indicate that AI research in K–12 education is evolving toward more pedagogically grounded, ethically informed, and student-centred educational models while simultaneously highlighting challenges related to teacher readiness, curriculum adaptation, and equitable AI integration in school contexts.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Background Bone metastasis represents a major complication of advanced malignancies and is associated with substantial skeletal morbidity, impaired quality of life, and complex clinical decision-making. Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly emerged as an important computational approach for analyzing heterogeneous biomedical data. The developmental landscape, intellectual evolution, and future clinical directions of artificial intelligence applications in bone metastasis remain insufficiently characterized. Methods A comprehensive bibliometric analysis was performed using publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed, and Scopus from January 2006 to June 2026. Bibliometric indicators, including annual publication trends, journal distribution, countries, institutions, authors, citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, thematic evolution, and reference bursts, were analyzed using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and R-based bibliometric tools. Results A total of 540 publications involving 3,439 authors from 237 journals were identified. Research output increased substantially after 2020, with an annual growth rate of 24.01%, reflecting rapid expansion of AI-related investigations in bone metastasis. China contributed the largest number of publications, whereas the United States, Japan, and European countries showed substantial scientific influence and international collaboration. Thematic analysis demonstrated a progressive transition from early computer-aided diagnosis and bone scintigraphy analysis toward deep learning, radiomics, multimodal prediction, and language-based artificial intelligence applications. Imaging-related approaches remained the dominant research direction, while emerging studies increasingly focused on clinical information extraction, prognostic modeling, and integration of heterogeneous data sources. A small number of recent studies explored language-based AI for clinical information extraction, data organization, and knowledge support, suggesting an emerging but still limited extension beyond conventional imaging applications. Conclusion AI research in bone metastasis has evolved from automated lesion recognition toward broader applications in disease characterization, risk assessment, and clinical decision support. Imaging, machine learning, deep learning, and radiomics remain the principal foundations of the field, whereas language-based AI currently represents a comparatively small and emerging research direction. Future studies should prioritize multicenter validation, multimodal data integration, prospective evaluation, and clinically meaningful endpoints. Large language model systems may warrant further investigation as potential components of future disease-specific AI frameworks, although their clinical utility in bone metastasis remains to be established.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare relies on diverse mathematical frameworks, yet their contributions to model development, evaluation, interpretability, and clinical translation remain fragmented. This systematic review synthesized the classical and emerging mathematical foundations underpinning healthcare AI and examined major methodological and application trends. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, studies published between January 2016 and June 30, 2026, were identified through systematic searches of Scopus, Google Scholar, and PubMed/MEDLINE, with searches conducted using Harzing’s Publish or Perish v8 where applicable. Bibliometric analysis was performed using VOSviewer, while methodological quality was assessed using an adapted JBI-based framework and AMSTAR-2 for systematic reviews. Of 653 records identified, 147 studies met the eligibility criteria. Non-mutually exclusive mathematical-domain coding identified linear algebra in 100/147 studies (68.0%), calculus and optimization in 91/147 (61.9%), and probability and statistics in 79/147 (53.7%), highlighting their roles in data representation, learning, optimization, inference, uncertainty quantification, and validation. A separate mutually exclusive classification of dominant methodological themes identified explainable and trustworthy AI in 24/147 studies (16.3%), statistics and learning theory in 23/147 (15.6%), probability and Bayesian methods in 23/147 (15.6%), calculus and optimization in 19/147 (12.9%), and linear algebra in 15/147 (10.2%). Radiology and medical imaging were the leading healthcare application (24.3%), while classification and diagnosis were the most frequent clinical task (17.1%). Overall, healthcare AI is supported by an interconnected mathematical ecosystem. Emerging approaches, including graph neural networks, Transformers, and quantum machine learning, require stronger external validation, standardized benchmarking, and rigorous evaluation for reliable clinical translation.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Background: Easy Mental Fatigability is an emerging clinical entity in modern occupational Health, characterized by rapid onset of mental exhaustion on/during/after cognitive tasks.In Ayurveda, this correlates with Manasika Glani, manifested as a result of Dhi-Dhriti-Smriti Vibhramsha occurred due to vridhdhi in Manas doshas Rajas and Tamas and Ojo-kshaya.Objective: To review classical Ayurveda concepts of Manasik Glani, its pathogenesis, Diagnostic features/symptoms, and management, and correlate with modern neuroscience.Methods: Ayurveda Classical texts Brattrayi and Laghutrrayi along with commentaries were screened.PubMed, Science Direct, DHARA, AYUSH Research Portal, Namaste Portal, Cochrane were searched for "Mental fatigue" AND "Ayurveda" from 2000-2005.Results: Manasik Glani results from Rajas-Tamas Vriddhi, Vata-Pitta Prakopa, and ojo-kshaya.Modern correlation includes impaired prefrontal cortex function, reduction in BDNF and HPA axis dysregulation.Yastmadhu, Bramhi and Shankhpushpi are the Medhya Rasayanas, have shown anti -fatigue actions via multiple pathways anti-oxidant, cholinergic, GABAergic and neuroplasticity pathways.Conclusion: Manasika Glani is a strong Ayurveda framework for Mental Fatigability.Integrated assessment using standardized and validated scales as CHQ, CIS-R etc. and Ayurveda symptoms of Manasik Glani, Dhi-Dhriti Vibransh are required.Also, Ayurveda assessment scale for Glani needs to be validated Also, clinical trials on Medhya Rasayana with large sample size are needed.

documents.abstract: Modern wide-field astronomical surveys are substantially increasing the volume of observational data and the discovery rate of near-Earth asteroids (NEAs), placing growing demands on efficient and automated initial orbit determination (IOD). The physics-informed extreme-learning machine (PIELM) is an artificial intelligence (AI)-based algorithm for IOD that reconstructs orbital trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. However, optical survey observations often span arcs that are too short to provide sufficient geometric constraints, making it difficult for the standard PIELM to determine a reliable initial orbit. New IOD methods capable of handling too-short arcs (TSAs) are therefore increasingly needed. We develop a new AI-based method for determining the initial orbits of NEAs from TSAs. It yields reliable initial estimates for subsequent least-squares refinement. We propose a metaheuristic PIELM method, termed MH-PIELM. An artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm explores candidate solutions defined by a single line-of-sight range, with PIELM embedded directly within the search to reconstruct the corresponding trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. The resulting PIELM loss serves as the fitness function, guiding the ABC algorithm toward promising candidate solutions. The method was tested on the initial optical observations reported for several NEAs. The MH-PIELM solutions enabled successful least-squares refinement, whose results closely agreed with the Jet Propulsion Laboratory reference solutions. The refined orbits were then used to predict the astrometric positions on the following day. Comparisons with the corresponding observations showed a useful short-term predictive capability for follow-up observations and target recovery, demonstrating the feasibility of the MH-PIELM approach. MH-PIELM offers a new AI-based strategy for initial orbit determination from TSAs by combining metaheuristic global search with physics-informed machine learning. It extends the applicability of the standard PIELM to challenging TSA observations.

Humans and intelligent systems are increasingly working together in high-stakes domains. To operate as real teammates, these systems require higher levels of autonomy, which is becoming increasingly feasible given rapid technological developments. Consequently, human-autonomy teaming (HAT) has become a key research area. Most HAT studies rely on simulation-based testbeds using simplified agents and tasks. These testbeds are often insufficiently flexible and customizable, limiting researchers in manipulating critical HAT attributes. Furthermore, most testbeds focus on dyadic teams, while real-world applications increasingly involve human interactions with multiple autonomous systems such as drone swarms. Understanding how operators can effectively control such swarms remains a critical challenge. During this demo, we will present our flexible and customizable HAT testbed, showing the example of human-swarm interaction during wildfire response. Attendees will experience controlling drone swarms with action-based and play-based control across varying swarm sizes, illustrating how the testbed facilitates systematic empirical research.

Research on why people contribute to open source software (OSS) and related open collaboration platforms spans more than two decades, but its findings conflict, and studies often treat the work people contribute and their intention to keep contributing as interchangeable. Drawing on self-determination theory and motivation crowding theory, we meta-analyze 41 studies. The main analysis pools 178 correlations of eight antecedents with contribution effort and continuance intention from 29 independent samples (N = 9,632). Seven antecedents relate positively to effort, all eight relate positively to intention, and each relates at least as strongly to intention as to effort. Contrary to a common assumption, intrinsic motivation is not more strongly related to effort than extrinsic motivation, but its gap between intention and effort is larger. Reputation relates to effort mainly on platforms with a reputation system, and we find no sign that monetary rewards crowd out enjoyment. The findings inform how platforms can turn contributors' intentions into work.

Groundwater irrigation quotas in agricultural multi-agent settings are typically computed against a known aquifer boundary, yet the boundary itself is an estimate whose uncertainty propagates into every quota decision. The framework separates two regret components: a boundary-regret term arising from mis-specified aquifer extent, and a coordination-regret term arising from the gap between the MARL equilibrium and the social optimum. A BACI design is then analysed under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, across cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, with 2000 replications per design cell. The design analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage-point effect at 80% power under this variance structure. The contribution is a formal bridge between MARL quota theory and the evaluation designs that would be needed to test it, together with an explicit statement of the boundary conditions under which welfare-regret bounds remain informative.

Understanding the historical allocation and distribution of research funding advances our knowledge of how scientific research is supported across fields, institutions, and regions. However, large-scale analyses are hindered by the lack of comprehensive funder name disambiguation solutions, as funder names often exhibit spelling variations, translations, abbreviations, and inconsistent levels of granularity. In this paper, we present a framework for developing multilingual, multi-functional funder name disambiguation models and demonstrate its application to research publications in biodiversity conservation. To construct a training dataset, we integrated the Research Organization Registry, which provides unique identifiers for research organizations, with two publication datasets: the Web of Science and the Crossref Open Funder Registry. We used multi-task learning with contrastive loss and multiple-negative ranking loss to fine-tune three open-weight embedding models from the Sentence Transformer, Gemma, and Qwen3 families. The best-performing models achieved accuracy above 0.90 when matching Web of Science funder names to Research Organization Registry identifiers, outperforming general-purpose large language models, including GPT-5.2, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, and Gemini-2.5-Flash, by more than 0.1. For funder names not indexed in the Research Organization Registry, we constructed a similarity network among funder names and identified clusters within it. Finally, we analyzed the disambiguation results and highlighted challenges arising from limited knowledge of smaller funders and funders from non-English-speaking countries. This work provides a reusable framework for funder name disambiguation with potential applicability across different model architectures and datasets, featuring cost-effective training data creation and multi-task learning and disambiguation.

Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality, yet the real-world performance of FDA-cleared AI detection models remains incompletely characterized. We retrospectively evaluated two FDA-cleared AI algorithms from a single commercial platform (Aidoc Medical BriefCase)—one for PE triage on dedicated CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA; n = 30,678) and one for incidental PE (iPE) detection on routine contrast-enhanced CTs ( n = 37,191), across a 17-facility academic health system. Reference-standard labels were extracted from radiology reports using a validated LLM pipeline (97% accuracy, κ = 0.94). The PE model achieved 86.8% sensitivity and 99.1% specificity, with sensitivity declining from 99.3% for saddle emboli to 72.9% for subsegmental PE, and from 89.7% for acute to 65.3% for non-acute PE. The iPE model achieved 73.5% sensitivity and 99.8% specificity. Both models demonstrated lower sensitivity than FDA-clearance benchmarks while exceeding cleared specificity, with diminishing performance for peripheral and non-acute emboli mirroring known human reader limitations and underscoring the need for standardized post-market surveillance of AI-enabled medical devices.
